name: Daily High Temperature — Bucket Forecast
description: Price every temperature bucket from ONE simulated distribution: a point forecast plus a fat-tailed historical forecast-error distribution gives the day's actual high; each 2-degree bucket is an indicator metric on the same paths, so the bucket probabilities are internally consistent and sum to 1. The natural shape for range / bucket questions (temperature, CPI, jobs prints) — and the shape forecast_buckets.py records and resolves as a set.

context.decision: Given a 72°F point forecast, how is the probability mass spread across the 2-degree buckets for tomorrow's high?
context.what_good_looks_like: Bucket probabilities that sum to 1, each with a 95% interval narrow enough to be compared against an external baseline.

calibration.source: Day-ahead point forecast for the station (e.g. NWS forecast max). Replace per day.

Historical (actual - forecast) for day-ahead max temperature at the station: slight warm bias (+0.3°F), ~2°F typical absolute error, fat tails on frontal-passage days. Fit from the station's own history before use.
